publisher_scope: Publicly available Oil India Limited event reports and official supporting documents.

records.activity_context: Workover operations on a producing gas well.
event_mechanism: The well became suddenly active during workover operations.
Natural gas and condensate were released in an uncontrolled manner.
records.reported_narrative: Oil India reports that Baghjan Well No. 5 became active during workover operations on 27 May 2020 and released natural gas and condensate uncontrollably. The well caught fire on 9 June 2020. It was capped on 17 August and finally killed, with the fire completely doused, on 15 November 2020.

reported_consequences.fatality_detail: Two OIL fire-fighters died while escaping the sudden ignition on 9 June; OIL's report also records the death of another OIL officer in the line of duty on 9 September.

response_and_recovery: OIL, ONGC Crisis Management Team, Alert Disaster Control, Indian Army, district administration and other agencies supported the response.
Continuous water spraying and site-control measures were used.
A BOP stack was placed over the well on 17 August 2020.
Gas flow was diverted to the Baghjan EPS and flare pits on 13 September 2020.
A snubbing operation began on 8 November 2020 and the well was killed with brine solution on 15 November 2020.
The later OIL compliance report records bioremediation, plantation of 50,000 saplings and CCTV surveillance.

preliminary_authority_findings.finding: Deficiency in understanding the gravity of removing the BOP without a confirmed and tested secondary safety barrier.
Preliminary material identifies deficiencies in planning, execution, adherence to procedure and supervision of the critical operation.

source_discrepancies: The OIL News narrative identifies two fire-fighter deaths on 9 June and one additional officer death on 9 September; the OISD report summarizes this as three employee deaths.

records.report_title: Incident at OIL well plinth NHK 162
records.activity_context: Bleeding hydrotest water through a 2-inch bleed line.
records.event_mechanism: While a 2-inch valve fitted to an artery-line connection was being opened, the valve and bleed line unexpectedly dislodged.
records.reported_narrative: OIL reported that the dislodged valve and bleed line caused fatal injury to a contractor employee working nearby. The employee was taken to OIL Hospital at Duliajan but died at approximately 5:00 pm on 14 February 2024.
response_and_investigation: The employee was taken immediately to OIL Hospital at Duliajan.
OIL stated that it would take measures to prevent recurrence.

records.activity_context: Wellsite production equipment at the X-mass tree.
records.event_mechanism: A hole was observed on the flow path from the X-mass tree, causing leakage of gas and crude oil.
records.reported_narrative: OIL reported leakage at the X-mass tree of BGN#24. OIL personnel controlled the leak at approximately 2:20 am on 10 April 2024. Gas and crude oil spread across nearby areas within approximately 100 metres of the wellsite.

reported_consequences.release_note: The press release does not state a fatality or injury count.

response_and_investigation: The district administration was informed and officials attended the site.
Fire service was mobilized and kept on standby.
OIL formed an on-site assessment team and began remediation measures.
OIL announced an internal enquiry and stated that the well was controlled and closed.

data_quality.labels: No AI predictions, model scores, or expert SIF labels are included. SIF status remains unresolved.
data_quality.coverage_note: Public disclosures are selective and tend to emphasize major incidents. Internal OIL reports, near misses, unsafe acts and unsafe conditions are not included.
data_quality.document_note: The complete downloaded source documents remain available at the local_path values; this JSON stores normalized event facts and provenance rather than duplicating every page of the source PDFs.
